scheme_name: PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana - Central Financial Assistance to Residential Consumers (capex mode)
description: The same PM Surya Ghar CFA at the higher special-category rates: Rs 33,000 per kWp for the first 2 kWp and Rs 19,800 for the third kWp; nothing beyond 3 kWp. Applies only in the special-category States/UTs named in clause 5(g) of the MNRE guideline.

source.name: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE), Government of India
source.document: Guidelines for PM-Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana - Central Financial Assistance to Residential Consumers (OM No. 318/17/2024-GCRT dated 07.06.2024, published on MNRE 02.07.2024)
source.table: Clause 5(h) 'Effective CFA' table, column 'CFA (Special Category States)'
source.section: Clause 5(g) Benchmark Cost; clause 5(h) Effective CFA
source.excerpt: Clause 5(g): The benchmark for special category States (States/UTs of Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, J&K, Ladakh, States in the North East including Sikkim, UTs of A&N and Lakshadweep) will be Rs 55,000 for first 2 kW of RTS capacity and Rs 49,500 for the additional kW of RTS capacity. Clause 5(h) CFA (Special Category States): first 2 kWp Rs 33,000/kWp; additional 1 kWp Rs 19,800/kWp; additional RTS capacity beyond 3 kWp: No additional CFA.

verification_notes: Rates read directly from the MNRE guideline PDF (SHA-256 2de9b3faf765c18b...). The guideline lists categories, not names: 'States in the North East including Sikkim' is applied as the eight NE States (Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Tripura, Sikkim). The maximum for a 3 kW system (2 x 33,000 + 19,800 = Rs 85,800) is derived arithmetic that the guideline does not state, so maximum_amount is left empty and the slab calculation produces it. See the PMSG-CFA-2024.02-STANDARD row for the amendment check (OM dated 13.02.2025 changes no amount), the 2026 status check and the stacking basis.
